headline: KSE-100 gave back some of Monday's rally Tuesday Aug 4 — down ~0.3% intraday to ~177,623 — after fresh Middle East attacks shattered the US-Iran peace hopes that drove Monday's jump; profit-taking hit banks, cement, autos, E&P. Portfolio value ~Rs 9.75M, P/L +Rs 251K (+2.64%) on cost, per Mali's price feed (updated 09:23 UTC today). Drawdown from the Jan ATH is ~6.3%, still well short of the 10% deploy-dry-powder line. AVN's sell-half plan was due at "Monday Aug 3's open" — that day has now passed and holdings still show the full 24,500 shares; this is the sixteenth straight review flagging it. EFERT's confirmed H1 2026 dividend record date (Rs 1.75/share) is Mon Aug 10 — 6 days out, not yet in the 3-day notification window. Technical note: all 8 scraped mutual-fund NAVs (ASSF, AKDISSF, NISIF, NISF, MIF, AICF, MICF, AKDISIF) have been frozen at identical values since Jul 24-25 — 8-9 straight trading days unchanged, despite the app claiming last review that this was resolved. A direct fetch of the MUFAP source page from this review returned HTTP 403, which strongly suggests mufap.com.pk is blocking the GitHub Actions runner's IP and the scraper has been silently failing every run since — the 9 fund holdings' displayed P/L is stale by over a week. Flagged as a follow-up code task; not something advice.json can fix.
market: PSX reversed course Tuesday: after Monday's 1.2% geopolitics-driven rally, the KSE-100 shed nearly 600 points intraday (as much as ~800-1,900 at various points during the session per wire reports) to trade around 177,623 (previous close 178,200.02), down roughly 0.3%, as fresh attacks in the Middle East reignited the same US-Iran tension that had just eased — automobile assemblers, cement, commercial banks, oil & gas exploration, refinery and power generation all saw selling, with some profit-taking on top after Monday's gains. Against the Jan 23, 2026 all-time high of 189,556, the drawdown widens slightly to roughly 6.3% — still well clear of the 10% line that would trigger deploying the AICF/MICF cash reserve; no change to the dry-powder plan. SBP's policy rate remains at 11.5% (held Jul 27, second consecutive pause); headline inflation eased to 11.1% in June; the IMF EFF/RSF program stays on track (~$4.8B disbursed to date, reserves ~$16B and rebuilding) — stable macro backdrop, nothing new. Mali's price feed (data/prices.json stamped 2026-08-04T09:23:25Z) shows no single holding moving more than ~1% day-over-day: AVN Rs 31.50 (flat, still lagging), MEBL Rs 572.45 (new high for the position, +0.6%), EFERT Rs 187.70 (-1.4%). Portfolio: cost basis Rs 9,493,504, current value (holdings + cash) ~Rs 9,748,398, unrealized P/L +Rs 250,615 (+2.64%) — down slightly from +2.75% yesterday, tracking the market pullback. On holdings: EFERT's Rs 1.75/share interim dividend ex-date is confirmed Aug 10, 2026 (payment Sep 3) — 6 days out, still outside the 3-day notify window; H1 results (profit -15.9% YoY consolidated, -34.6% YoY standalone) already confirmed last review, nothing new since. AVN: no fresh company news found (no board meeting, no director dealing, no earnings surprise) — the position is exactly where it was, still the full 24,500 shares, one day past the stated "Monday Aug 3's open" execution window with no update to holdings. Either the trade happened off-app and index.html needs updating, or it's still pending — sixteen straight reviews is well past the point of this being a live decision rather than a stale one. AVN's Sep 2, 2026 earnings remains the outside deadline for a full exit if there's still no recovery. CPHL: no update since the Jul 8 REIT-demerger board approval — still a value-unlock story in motion, subject to shareholder/court/regulatory approval, no urgency either way. Technical note (see headline): the fund-NAV feed has been stuck since Jul 24-25 across all 8 MUFAP-scraped tickers, and a direct fetch of the MUFAP source during this review returned HTTP 403 — the earlier "resolved" call in the Aug 3 review was wrong; this looks like the runner's IP got blocked, not a transient blip. Stock prices (dps.psx.com.pk) are unaffected and still updating normally.

actions.title: Engro Fertilizers — H1 results confirmed: real earnings decline, dividend still paid
actions.detail: −5.7% on cost (Rs 187.70 today, -1.4% on the day, giving back yesterday's bounce). Confirmed H1 2026 results (PSX filing, Jul 30): consolidated profit Rs 7.12B (-15.9% YoY), EPS Rs 5.33 (vs Rs 6.34) — standalone was worse, profit -34.6% YoY, EPS Rs 4.49 (vs Rs 6.87) — cushioned at the consolidated level by a one-off Rs 1.8B SIDC remeasurement gain that won't repeat. This confirms the glut thesis rather than reversing it: H1 urea sales hit a 10-year low at 537,000 tons, inventory swollen to 694,000 tons, discounts fully withdrawn Apr 4 (market share ~27%), new CEO Imran Ahmed (joined May 11) now delivering his first full set of weak numbers. The board still declared an interim dividend of Rs 1.75/share (17.5%) on top of the Rs 2.00/share (20%) already paid this year — yield is intact for now, ex-date confirmed Mon Aug 10, 2026 (payment Sep 3, now 6 days out). Keep for yield given the dividend held up, but this is now the second straight half with declining core earnings — rotate out if Q3/Q4 offtake doesn't recover or the next dividend gets cut outright.
